summary.headline: Zydus Wellness Q1 FY27 consolidated net sales rose 66.7% YoY to INR 14,299 million, with EBITDA up 55.3% to INR 2,417 million, while reported net profit fell 7%.
summary.overview: Consolidated sales grew 66.7% YoY to INR 14,299 million, helped by the Comfort Click consolidation, with EBITDA up 55.3% to INR 2,417 million and EBITDA margin up about 0.4% on a like-to-like basis. Reported net profit declined 7%, but profit excluding amortisation of acquired brands grew 26.5%. The domestic business grew 4.6%, with Skin & Hair Care up 34.5% and Food & Nutrition up 16%, while seasonal brands fell 12% due to unseasonal rains in the East and North. International (including Comfort Click) grew 24.8% like-to-like, and management said the summer weakness was recovering in the second half of the quarter.

financial_highlights.change: Core like-for-like described as similar to last year

segments.name: Skin and Hair Care (domestic)
segments.commentary: Grew 34.5% in the quarter. Everyuth delivered strong double-digit growth, with its facial cleansing rank improving from fifth to fourth and tan removal ahead of internal expectations.

segments.name: Food and Nutrition (domestic)
segments.commentary: Grew 16%. Complan grew faster than the prior quarter despite category degrowth; RiteBite Max Protein grew more than double its historical rate; Nutralite delivered strong growth.

segments.name: Seasonal brands (domestic)
segments.commentary: Declined 12% on a softer summer. Nycil was hit hardest by North and East rains and retailer inventory; Glucon-D was flattish as East offset gains elsewhere.

segments.name: International incl. Comfort Click
segments.commentary: Like-to-like growth of 24.8%. Comfort Click carries much higher margins and is EPS accretive; launched WeightWorld D2C in the US, Walmart marketplace, and noon UAE with a physical UAE base.

guidance_outlook: International growth: management said it will maintain its 'double-digit' framing and declined to give forward-looking numbers.
Comfort Click: management expects continued EPS accretion and margin improvement if the current momentum holds, despite the seasonally weak September and December quarters.
Effective tax rate: Q1 ETR near 27% due to UK thin-cap disallowances (about 25% underlying). For FY27, about 12-15 points of the 25% are cash; from FY28 the full 25% is expected to be cash.
Finance cost: lower after switching the GBP loan to a euro loan at a much lower rate; the run-rate is expected to hold unless euro benchmark rates move significantly.
Seasonal brands: management expects a positive trajectory for the rest of the year; trade inventory is said to be no higher than last year and the product shelf life is three years.
capex_capacity: Comfort Click costs: an analyst cited about INR 80-85 crore a quarter of interest and depreciation, which management did not dispute.

New launches: Complan Power Play RTD milkshake (vanilla and chocolate, no added sugar), VieMax Diabetes Care, and additional RiteBite Max Protein range (millet wafer bar, Roots, Korean chips, RTDs, cookies).
Comfort Click support and service teams remain in India even as operations expand into the US and Middle East.
Management said more launches are coming in the next few quarters, with a long-term pipeline described as robust for two to three years.
demand_pricing: Consumer demand held up, with spending shifting towards premium products; quick commerce and e-commerce remain the primary growth engines with strong double-digit growth.
Pricing discipline, mix improvement and premium offerings offset input cost volatility, which management described as manageable.
Core gross margin expansion stayed strong, with additional margin support from Comfort Click.
Geopolitical disruption: management said the company's impact was limited to mitigation measures.
Nycil faced channel destocking and slower uptake because of high retailer inventory from the prior year; management said it expects a more positive finish to the year.

qa_highlights.question: Was international growth constrained by stock availability or supply chain issues?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no specific constraints; 25% is a good growth rate, but it will keep guiding to double-digit growth and does not give forward-looking numbers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the effective tax rate outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 ETR was near 27% (about 25% underlying, distorted by UK thin-cap disallowances). For FY27, 12-15 points of the 25% are cash; from FY28 it is expected to be fully cash.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost fall QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: The GBP loan was refinanced into a euro loan at a much lower rate; the finance cost run-rate should hold unless the euro benchmark moves materially.

qa_highlights.question: What was the 12% seasonal decline by geography?
qa_highlights.answer: East (continuous April-May rain) and North were the main drags. Glucon-D's gains in North, West and South were offset by East. Nycil was hit by North and East plus retailer stock. Growth recovered in the second half of the quarter but not enough to offset the full-quarter drag.

qa_highlights.question: Will Comfort Click be EBITDA-positive in the seasonally weak September and December quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Comfort Click has been EPS accretive since Q4 FY26 and expects net margin, EBITDA and PBT to rise if momentum continues. Comfort Click's US presence is 'very small' but growing well and is too early to judge.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Complan's growth despite category degrowth?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth came from the core kids segment (better nutrition, advertising, distribution), celebrity endorsement, toddler (NutriGro), adult nutrition (VieMax, VieMax Diabetes Care) and RTD entry (Complan Power Play). Kids nutrition is the core driver.

qa_highlights.question: What were A&P spends and digital mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Reported A&P was 18.2% of total sales, including Comfort Click, which spends heavily on advertising. Like-for-like core A&P was similar to last year. Digital's share of spend is rising.

risks_watch: Seasonal brands: Nycil and Glucon-D weakness in East and North, with retailer inventory from last year still weighing; management expects a more positive finish but the full-year recovery is not yet proven.
Comfort Click profitability in seasonally weak September and December quarters, given about INR 80-85 crore a quarter of interest and depreciation (analyst estimate, not disputed by management).
Tax: Q1 ETR near 27% from UK thin-cap disallowances; FY27 cash tax covers only about 12-15 of the 25 points, with full cash tax expected from FY28.
International growth: management declined to give forward numbers and will only guide to double-digit growth, despite about 25% like-to-like growth in Q1.
Finance cost: run-rate depends on euro benchmark rates after the GBP-to-euro loan switch.
Reported net profit fell 7% in Q1 even as EBITDA rose 55.3%; the gap is attributed to amortisation of acquired brands.
key_quotes: 25% is a good growth. We've been talking about our double-digit growth.
We normally don't give a forward-looking. We just said double digits, so that's what we will maintain.
Our own inventory is not more than what it was last year, probably a bit lower.
Too early to predict, but right now very very small, but growing well.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the core and international business, citing a 25% like-to-like international growth rate and strong Food and Skin care growth. It was cautious and evasive on forward numbers, declining to give forward-looking figures for international growth and Comfort Click, and on the Nycil and seasonal recovery it said the numbers "will have to play out".
